analysis.title: The great rotation
key_insights: The Russell 2000 has sharply outperformed the Nasdaq over the past month, one of the largest relative rotations in years, with small caps acting as the place to hide from the tech selloff.
Small-cap outperformance has moved in lockstep with falling yields. The note credits BTIG's Krinsky with calling this.
The Nasdaq 100 had its worst monthly underperformance versus the equal-weighted S&P 500 since 2002.
AI versus AI at Risk (GSPUARTI, a Goldman Sachs basket pair) had its second-worst monthly performance since ChatGPT launched.

The Russell/NDX ratio has risen in one of its most aggressive moves in several years, but the longer-term downtrend in the ratio remains intact. The note frames this as either a historic rotation or a violent countertrend rally.
Russell volatility has stayed contained during the tech selloff, so relative fear in tech is high compared with the broader market.
NDX is testing its longer-term trend line and 200-day moving average. The note asks whether shorts pressed into this support get squeezed.
Tech P/E multiples have compressed to levels not seen in some time, so the relative valuation case for tech is improving even as investors exit.

Bottom line: the Russell revival is real, but the rotation looks stretched. With tech at major support, valuations reset and relative fear near extremes, the risk of a sharp reversal is rising. Chasing small-cap outperformance now may be as risky as chasing tech at the highs.

sector_views.rationale: Selloff is testing the 200-day moving average and trend line, multiples have compressed, and relative fear is high, which the note says raises the risk of a squeeze higher.
Outperformance is described as real but stretched, and chasing it is called potentially as dangerous as chasing tech at the highs.

risk_factors: Rotation into small caps has become stretched, and a sharp reversal back toward tech is possible.
Chasing small-cap outperformance at this point carries risk comparable to chasing tech at the highs.
Continued falling yields are the driver of small-cap strength, so a reversal in yields would hurt that trade.
